metas.name: Whiplash
metas.description:
Ambition becomes a kind of self-violence. A jazz drummer practises until his hands bleed under a teacher who terrorises him, and the final scene shows the exact moment he chooses greatness anyway, without resolving whether it was worth it.

A promising young drummer enrolls at a cut-throat music conservatory where his dreams of greatness are mentored by an instructor who will stop at nothing to realize a student's potential.

metas.name: Stop Making Sense
metas.description:
This is a band building joy in real time. A Talking Heads concert that starts with David Byrne alone with a boombox and adds one musician per song until the stage is full — and his suit keeps getting bigger.

A live performance of the band Talking Heads shot over the course of three nights at Hollywood's Pantages Theater in December of 1983 and featuring their most memorable songs.

metas.name: Amazing Grace
metas.description:
Aretha Franklin's singing here is spiritual labour. She records a live gospel album in a Los Angeles church in 1972, over two nights, in a performance that visibly costs her something.

A documentary presenting Aretha Franklin with choir at the New Bethel Baptist Church in Watts, Los Angeles in January 1972.

metas.name: Summer of Soul
metas.description:
A community's archive sat in a basement for 50 years. What it held was the 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival — Stevie Wonder, Nina Simone, Mahalia Jackson, Sly Stone — in footage almost nobody saw.

Documentary about the legendary 1969 Harlem Cultural Festival which celebrated African-American music and culture and promoted Black pride and unity.

metas.name: The Last Waltz
metas.description:
A musical era ends on stage here, politely. The Band's farewell concert with everyone they came up with as guests, and backstage interviews with men who sound relieved and bereaved at once.

A film account and presentation of the final concert of The Band.

metas.name: Buena Vista Social Club
metas.description:
Elderly Cuban son musicians — some retired to shining shoes — are found again, recording and touring after years away; the pleasure is in their faces and Havana's streets.

A group of elder forgotten Cuban music legends emerge from obscurity when an American producer reunites them in Havana, leading to spectacular performances that reignite their musical legacy.

metas.name: 20 Feet from Stardom
metas.description:
The voices you know best belong to people you can't name. Backup singers for the Stones, Springsteen and Sting — huge talent, a career spent three steps behind someone else.

Backup singers live in a world that lies just beyond the spotlight. Their voices bring harmony to the biggest bands in popular music, but we've had no idea who these singers are or what lives they lead, until now.

metas.name: Koyaanisqatsi
metas.description:
Civilisation itself becomes pattern. No dialogue or characters: time-lapse clouds, highways, factories, demolition and crowds cut to Philip Glass, until modern life starts to look like weather.

A collection of expertly photographed phenomena with no conventional plot. The footage focuses on the relationship between nature, humanity, and technology.

metas.name: Singin' in the Rain
metas.description:
Pure performed joy, inside a story about an industry panicking. Hollywood switching to sound, a star with a terrible voice, and musical numbers that still feel like showing off for the love of it.

When Hollywood's silent era gives way to talkies, a dashing screen idol and a gifted newcomer navigate romance, rivalry, and the comic chaos of reinventing the movies.

metas.name: Tár
metas.description:
Prestige is a system one woman believes she controls. A conductor at the top of classical music — Berlin, Mahler, acolytes — and a slow accumulation of recordings, edits and allegations, filmed with the cold precision its subject would admire.

Set in the international world of Western classical music, the film centers on Lydia Tár, widely considered one of the greatest living composer-conductors and the very first female director of a major German orchestra.

metas.name: Sound of Metal
metas.description:
Hearing loss is rendered from inside the head. A metal drummer goes deaf and the sound design puts you in his skull — muffled, ringing — then the strange peace of a deaf community that doesn't treat deafness as damage.

A drummer begins to experience hearing loss and fears for his music career.

metas.name: Gimme Shelter
metas.director: Albert Maysles, David Maysles, Charlotte Zwerin
metas.description:
The 1960s dream curdles in a single precise frame: Altamont, a fan stabbed to death in front of the stage, and the Rolling Stones afterwards watching the footage of it, not knowing what to say.

When three hundred thousand members of the Love Generation collided with a few dozen Hells Angels at San Francisco's Altamont Speedway, the bloody slash that transformed a decade's dreams into disillusionment was immortalized on t...

metas.name: Amy
metas.description:
The machinery of fame eats a person whose talent is right there on screen the whole time. Amy Winehouse's rise and destruction assembled from home video, voicemails and the tabloid footage that hunted her.

Archival footage and personal testimonials present an intimate portrait of the life and career of British singer/songwriter Amy Winehouse.

metas.name: Searching for Sugar Man
metas.description:
Fame exists in full, in a place the famous person never knew about. Detroit singer Rodriguez, a flop at home in the 1970s and rumoured dead, was bigger than Elvis in apartheid South Africa. Sheer joy, start to finish.

Two South Africans set out to discover what happened to their unlikely musical hero, the mysterious 1970s rock n roller, Rodriguez.

metas.name: Dont Look Back
metas.description:
Pennebaker films celebrity as combat sport, at the moment it was invented. Inside Dylan's 1965 England tour: the cue-card sequence, Dylan dismantling journalists in hotel rooms, a persona manufactured in front of the lens.

Documentary covering Bob Dylan's 1965 tour of England, which includes appearances by Joan Baez and Donovan.

metas.name: The Piano
metas.description:
Campion conducts desire entirely through objects, landscape and music. Her mute Scottish bride arrives in colonial New Zealand, and her piano, left on the beach by her husband, becomes the currency of a wordless negotiation in bush and mud that feel mythic.

In the mid-19th century a mute woman is sent to New Zealand along with her young daughter and prized piano for an arranged marriage to a farmer, but is soon lusted after by a farm worker.

metas.name: Yellow Earth
metas.description:
A folk culture so total becomes the cinematography itself. A Communist soldier arrives in a loess-plateau village in 1939 to collect folk songs for the army, and finds a girl whose singing is the only free thing in her life.

A communist soldier is sent to a remote region of China in order to collect folk songs. Staying with a peasant family (a widower with two small children), he discovers a community whose way of life is completely alien to him, but he gradually wins their trust.

metas.name: The Travelling Players
metas.description:
A nation's history is carried here by the people paid to keep entertaining it. Angelopoulos follows a folk theatre troupe performing the same pastoral play across Greece from 1939 to 1952, and in vast single takes, occupation, civil war and executions slide past mid-scene.

Greece, 1939-1952: Fascist, Nazi, and Communist conflict, as seen through the eyes of a family of travelling provincial players.

metas.name: Once
metas.description:
Two musicians in Dublin fall into perfect collaboration and decline, kindly, to wreck their lives with it. A busker and a Czech pianist make an album in a week; the love is real, expressed entirely as music, and the ending honours everyone including the people not in the room. Shot on a camcorder for almost nothing.

A modern-day musical about a busker and an immigrant and their eventful week in Dublin, as they write, rehearse and record songs that tell their love story.

metas.name: Billy Elliot
metas.description:
A miner's son's body insists on ballet during the strike that is crushing his father. The body in health, at last: dancing as the one articulate thing in a house of men who can't talk. And the father's thaw — pride arriving through sacrifice he never announces — is a reconciliation of a kind rarely granted.

A talented young boy becomes torn between his unexpected love of dance and the disintegration of his family.

metas.name: This Is Spinal Tap
metas.description:
A metal band's decline is documented with total, lethal courtesy. This is a satire and also the music-industry film — amps to eleven, drummers expiring, a Stonehenge set built to the wrong unit. The mockumentary form does the rest: every interview projects a band that no longer exists.

Spinal Tap, one of England's loudest bands, is chronicled by film director Marty DiBergi on what proves to be a fateful tour.

metas.name: The Band's Visit
metas.description:
An Egyptian police orchestra spends one night stranded in the wrong Israeli town, and enmity dissolves into dinner, small talk and a roller rink. Reconciliation without a summit — just people feeding their assigned enemies. A very quiet film, and one where music does diplomacy's job.

A band comprised of members of the Egyptian police force head to Israel to play at the inaugural ceremony of an Arab arts center, only to find themselves lost in the wrong town.

metas.name: Pina
metas.description:
Dance becomes a language for things speech handles badly. Pina Bausch's company performs her pieces — in a theatre, on a traffic island, in a quarry, beside a tram line — shortly after her sudden death, the dancers' faces held in close-up between numbers. Shot in 3D that for once serves the subject: bodies occupying real space, at full scale.

A tribute to the late German choreographer Pina Bausch, as her dancers perform her most famous creations.

metas.name: We Are the Best!
metas.description:
Three thirteen-year-olds form a punk band to prove a point nobody asked them to prove. Stockholm, 1982: two girls who can't play recruit a quiet Christian guitarist, rehearse a song called "Hate the Sport" in a youth centre, and are simply, enormously alive. Adolescence as joy rather than damage — energy of a kind usually drawn from destruction, here from two chords and total conviction.

Three girls in 1980s Stockholm decide to form a punk band -- despite not having any instruments and being told by everyone that punk is dead.

metas.name: You, the Living
metas.description:
Ordinary misery is arranged into perfect tableaux. Fifty short scenes — a psychiatrist who's stopped believing, a girl dreaming of marrying a rock star, a carpet seller, a tuba ruining a marriage — shot in fixed frames of grey-green precision, each a small diorama of someone waiting for life to start. Deadpan as compassion: nobody is mocked, everybody is framed beautifully, nothing is resolved.

Humankind's greatness, baseness, joy, sorrow, self-confidence, anxiety, desire to love and be loved.
